units.spine: The market is open, and the carts stop where the stalls stand.
Every rule here has a room it is kept in, and every room has its clerk.
People here can afford to argue about something other than money.
Nothing about this ground argues against a town standing on it.
The walls are sound, the watch is kept, and neither is for show.
Nobody expects the town to lose a straight fight.
The beasts of this ground are met by the watch and by whoever takes a charter for the work, and the tools for it are kept ready.
The main streets are kept in order, and less is asked of the lanes behind them.
Prices hold steady, and the place does not live on the last thing that sold.
The town keeps no one on for magic, and what it wants of it is sent for from outside.
The price of bread is watched, and by more people than the bakers.
The Governing Council and The Order of the Watch are careful with each other, and what stands between them in Spitzplatz is political influence.
The road runs past the town, and the town takes little from what passes on it.
What the town cannot grow comes in by the road.
Spitzplatz is a town in the ordinary sense, and the word is accurate.
One tie here carries more weight than the rest, and the weight shows in what the town does and does not do.
The ties in the town are the ordinary ones, made by work, by family, and by living on the same street.
